# Does changing wording change human behavior predictions?

2026-11-26 | Anicca Research

**TL;DR.** We evaluated 5,120 prompts on four fixed checkpoints. Base canonical 0.5351, ensemble 0.3167, raw range 0.0149; Weighted SFT canonical 0.5466, ensemble 0.3269, raw range 0.0151; DPO canonical 0.4227, ensemble 0.2324, raw range 0.0265; DPO + consistency canonical 0.5658, ensemble 0.3487, raw range 0.0176. No promotion.

![cover](/assets/research/manager-execution-05-prompt-robustness-2026-11-26-cover.svg)

Cover: Run05 test n=96, 9 positive.

## The problem
Order averaging alone does not guarantee wording robustness. This benchmark note is for ML engineers familiar with binary prediction.

## How we did it
4 fixed checkpoints (base and Run04 seed42 adapters), 4 hand-written templates (canonical, EN paraphrase, JP question only, JP full), both answer orders, same 96 test cases (9 positive), calibration64, 5120 prompt evaluations. Canonical calibration fitted once and transferred across all variants; ensemble uses separate fit on same calibration split. No new training. Own-pilot disjoint test; global overlap unknown. Full Japanese changes both context language and option labels, not an isolated language intervention. No independent translation adjudication. Mean range is mean(max p - min p), not POSIX. Equal averaging is not Bayesian prompt ensembling. Small sample, no official external score or promotion.

![pipeline](/assets/research/manager-execution-05-prompt-robustness-2026-11-26-pipeline.svg)

Figure 1. Four checkpoints, four templates, two orders, 64 calibration and 96 test sessions.

## Results
| Model | Canonical AUC | EN paraphrase | JP question | JP full | Ensemble AUC | Raw range | Calibrated range |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Base | 0.53512 | 0.35121 | 0.44189 | 0.32439 | 0.31673 | 0.01493 | 0.00886 |
| Weighted SFT | 0.54662 | 0.36015 | 0.42656 | 0.32695 | 0.32695 | 0.01511 | 0.00896 |
| DPO | 0.42273 | 0.21584 | 0.39080 | 0.27203 | 0.23244 | 0.02651 | 0.02130 |
| DPO + consistency | 0.56577 | 0.39080 | 0.43934 | 0.33333 | 0.34866 | 0.01756 | 0.01013 |

![chart](/assets/research/manager-execution-05-prompt-robustness-2026-11-26-chart.svg)

Figure 2. Actual AUROC by template and ensemble, same 96 cases. [Receipt and audit](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca/pull/9519). All 40 AUROC and Brier values independently recomputed; 2,000 paired stratified draws per comparison.

## Trade-offs and unverified items
Four-template ensembling costs eight evaluations per case instead of two for one template. We used only seed42 adapters and 9 positive test labels. Calibration can compress differences without fixing ranking. No official benchmark, causal effect, multilingual generalization or user benefit established. Full Japanese changes label language too.

## Reproduce or contribute
[Code and predictions](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca/pull/9519); propose independent bilingual template adjudication and larger matched evaluation.
